package_info.package_versions: Magento 1 (all versions, as platform is end-of-life)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected code is designed to steal payment card data from customers by skimming sensitive information during checkout and exfiltrating it to an attacker-controlled domain. The code is loaded via a compromised third-party domain and leverages SQL and PHP object injection to gain control of the store, enabling persistent and covert theft of payment data.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a customer loads the checkout page
execution_context.file_location: Injected into Magento 1 frontend template files (e.g., app/design/frontend/base/default/template/checkout/onepage.phtml) or JavaScript files (e.g., skin/frontend/base/default/js/), via SQL or PHP object injection
required_permissions: network (to load external scripts and exfiltrate data)
filesystem (write access to web files for code injection)

malicious_snippets.code_language: JavaScript (injected via PHP/SQL into Magento templates or JS files)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the checkout page is loaded, the code injects a remote JavaScript file from https://naturalfreshmall.com/skin/frontend/base/default/js/payment.js, which programmatically captures sensitive payment form data entered by customers, transmits this data via HTTP requests to the attacker's server, and results in the exfiltration of payment card information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code loads JavaScript from an unrelated, external domain (naturalfreshmall.com) directly on the payment checkout page, which is a hallmark of Magecart-style skimming attacks. This domain is not associated with the legitimate business and is used to deliver malicious scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Magento stores should only load scripts from trusted, first-party domains or well-known third-party providers (such as payment processors or analytics platforms). Injecting arbitrary third-party scripts into sensitive payment workflows is never standard practice and violates PCI DSS requirements.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some stores legitimately use third-party scripts for analytics or payment processing, but these are from well-known, vetted domains (e.g., Google Analytics, Stripe, PayPal). Loading scripts from obscure or unrelated domains is not legitimate.
key_indicators: Presence of <script> tags referencing naturalfreshmall.com in checkout or payment-related templates
External JavaScript loaded from a domain with no legitimate business relationship
Script injection occurs specifically in sensitive payment workflow files
No corresponding legitimate extension or module for the loaded script

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits SQL injection and PHP object injection vulnerabilities in the Magento 1 store to gain unauthorized write access to web application files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify frontend template or JavaScript files, enabling persistent code injection

attack_chain.action: Malicious <script> tag referencing the attacker's domain is injected into the checkout page or related frontend files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of remote JavaScript code in customer browsers during checkout

attack_chain.action: Remote JavaScript skimmer, loaded from the attacker's domain, captures payment form data entered by customers and exfiltrates it to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Theft of customer payment card information, enabling financial fraud

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected external JavaScript loaded on checkout or payment pages, especially from domains not associated with the business
Network requests from customer browsers to untrusted or previously unseen domains during the checkout process
Unauthorized or unexplained modifications to Magento frontend template or JavaScript files outside of normal update cycles
file_indicators: Injected <script> tags referencing https://naturalfreshmall.com/skin/frontend/base/default/js/payment.js in template files (e.g., onepage.phtml)
Unusual changes or additions in skin/frontend/base/default/js/ or app/design/frontend/base/default/template/checkout/ files
Presence of new or modified files that include external script references in payment-related templates
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP or HTTPS connections from customer browsers to naturalfreshmall.com during checkout
POST or GET requests containing payment or form data sent to external domains not associated with the merchant
DNS lookups for naturalfreshmall.com originating from the checkout page
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to Magento frontend template and JavaScript files, especially those that add or modify <script> tags referencing external domains. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to detect and block SQL injection and PHP object injection attempts. Analyze network traffic from checkout pages for requests to untrusted domains such as naturalfreshmall.com. Regularly scan the page source code for the presence of known skimmer domains and unexpected external script inclusions. Implement file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized file changes in payment workflow files.
